This site presents the initial version of the database design and its potential applications using the publicly available [4Demon](https://www.vliz.be/projects/4demon/index.htm) dataset.

{{< include _generations.qmd >}}

## Source Data

-  [Four Decades of Belgian Marine Monitoring (4Demon)](https://www.vliz.be/projects/4demon/index.htm)

### Count of Sediment Sites
The table below summarizes the number of sediment sites collected across five projects between 1978 and 2015.

{{< include _db-setup.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| output: false

aq = require("arquero")

// --- Query: long format counts per cruise type, year, and element ---
counts_long = db.query(`
    SELECT project,
           CAST(CAST(year AS INTEGER) AS TEXT) AS year,
           UPPER(SUBSTR(parameter_name, 1, 1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(parameter_name, 2)) AS parameter_name,
           count(*) AS count
    FROM sediment s1
    JOIN sample s2 ON s2.sample_id = s1.sample_id
    JOIN station s3 ON s3.station_id = s2.station_id
    JOIN project p1 ON p1.project_id = s2.project_id
    JOIN parameter p2 ON p2.parameter = s1.parameter
    WHERE s1.parameter in ('CU', 'ZN')
    GROUP BY project, year, parameter_name
`)

// --- Pivot to wide format using Arquero ---
elements_wide = ["Copper", "Zinc"]

counts_wide = aq.from(counts_long)
  .groupby("project", "year")
  .pivot("parameter_name", "count")
  .orderby("project", "year")
  .rename({ project: "Project", year: "Year" })
  .objects()
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(counts_wide, {
  columns: ["Project", "Year", ...elements_wide],
  layout: "auto",
  rows: 20
})
```

## Database Design and Creation

After creating the ER (Entity–Relationship) diagram, the tables were implemented in a single SQLite file containing six tables. All required data were extracted from the 4Demon export file and imported into the corresponding tables.

- See the [DB Schema (Full)](./db-schema.qmd) page for details of the full database architecture.
- See the [Data Preparation](./data-preparation.qmd) page for the data preparation process used prior to importing the 4Demon dataset.
- See the [Database Downloads](./database-downloads.qmd) page for the download link to the SQLite database file.

## Geospatial Analysis

The pilot database reserves columns for the distance to the nearest coastline, the
nearest country and municipality, and the sea or ocean name, but leaves them empty.

They were derived here until August 2026, and the three pages that presented them
have been retired along with the calculation. The reason is that they never reached
any later stage: the clean generation recomputes all of them from the site
coordinates and overwrites whatever the pilot held, so deriving them twice produced
a second set of numbers that could only disagree with the ones that survive. The
values now live on the [multised-clean](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-clean/)
site.
